# create_workflow_artifact_tool

> File a structured-work pipeline deliverable as an organized, work-item-linked artifact (any domain).

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `workflow` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations; grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=create_workflow_artifact_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

File a structured-work pipeline deliverable as an organized, work-item-linked
artifact (any domain). Use this for a stage's deliverable, then pass the
returned id to orchestration_stage_complete_tool ({key, artifact_type: "llm_file",
llm_file_id: <id>}).

Saved at /workflow/<domain>/<work-item-type>/<id>-<slug>/<phase>/<title>.<md|html> and
attached to the work item — you never pass a directory_path. `phase` is free-form
(use your pipeline's stage/phase name, e.g. "compliance-matrix", "design", "outline").
FORMAT follows the ask: `markdown` (default) for anything the reader will READ (specs,
reviews, reports, plans); `html` for anything the reader will LOOK AT (dashboards, scorecards,
status boards) as ONE self-contained page — inline <style>, inline-SVG charts, no <script>.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `domain` | string | yes | Pipeline domain, e.g. "rfp", "book", "meeting-notes". Lowercase-kebab. |
| `work_item_type` | string | yes | "task" (Task), "ticket" (BizTxnEvent), "project" (Project), or "orchestration_execution" (the workflow run itself, for pipelines not rooted on a real work item). Use the value from your checkout work_item block. One of: `task`, `ticket`, `project`, `orchestration_execution`. |
| `work_item_id` | integer | yes | Numeric id of the work item. |
| `phase` | string | yes | Phase/stage name this artifact belongs to (free-form; your pipeline owns the vocabulary). |
| `title` | string | yes | Artifact title; also the filename stem. |
| `content` | string | yes | Body of the artifact, in the chosen format. |
| `format` | string | no | "markdown" (default) for prose deliverables; "html" for a self-contained visual page (dashboard, scorecard, status board). One of: `markdown`, `html`. |
